preconditions.description: Must be the current owner of the contract to call transferOwnership

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the current owner, call transferOwnership with address(0) as the new owner parameter. This will set the contract owner to the zero address, effectively locking ownership and preventing any future ownership transfers or privileged operations that require the owner role. The vulnerability is that the function doesn't validate that the new owner is a valid/externally owned account.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The SapToken contract inherits from Ownable which has a renounceOwnership() function that sets the owner to address(0) without any validation. This is a Pull-Over-Push vulnerability where privileged access can be permanently lost by transferring ownership to the zero address, effectively bricking the contract's administrative functions.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the current owner and call renounceOwnership() to set the owner to address(0), satisfying the oracle check that SapToken.owner() == address(0).
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the current owner address by calling owner() on the SapToken contract. 2. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the owner. 3. Call renounceOwnership() on the SapToken contract. 4. Verify that owner() now returns address(0).
